summary: Iter16 backend testing complete. All 16 tests pass covering AC/VE/FI auto entries (create/update/delete cleanup), manual-delete protection (400 on auto-generated), /api/fiscal/expenses shape+filters, and full regularization flow (dry_run + persist + delete) including reserve-not-extourned invariant. RBAC owner -> 403 confirmed on /expenses and /regularize. Regression: iter14 (8/8) + iter15 (16/16) still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: auto_entries.generate_sale_entry prorates the reserve across owners by the ratio reserve_total/full_total of each owner's total (line 138). This works only if the reserve line in fund_call.lines uses the SAME distribution key as the provisions line. If reserve uses a different key (as ReserveFund.distribution_key_id allows), the resulting VE entry will misattribute reserve per-owner amounts vs the actual fund_call.distribution. Recommend either: (a) record reserve_distribution separately on fund_call, OR (b) re-run distribution using the reserve key here. Functional impact: per-owner 40010XXX balances on the journal will differ from the actual reserve appel rows, even though the entry stays balanced.

auto_entries.generate_purchase_entry falls back to 'fournisseur 440000' when supplier has no tier account. But 440000 has NO copropriete scope and NO third_party_id, meaning the supplier sub-ledger (balance-tiers/suppliers) will miss this invoice. Recommend: always call assign_supplier_account when supplier doc is missing or auto-create a placeholder supplier so a 44000XXX is reserved per ACP. Today only suppliers explicitly created via /api/suppliers get a tier account.

routes/fiscal.py regularize_fiscal_year: total_real is computed from invoices.total_amount (line 199-206) but manual OD class-6 entries are ALSO summed (line 211-219). If an invoice's AC auto-entry is replayed and an admin re-categorizes via OD, both sources will double-count. Real-expenses by_owner _distribute is rebuilt from the invoice account_number + key only — manual OD entries are added to by_nature_key[(acc,'')] but NOT distributed to real_by_owner per owner (their amount goes only into total_real not into _distribute loop). Wait — looking again, line 273 loops over ALL by_nature_key including manual OD (with empty key_id), so they ARE distributed via default tantiemes. Fine. But the summary 'total_real_expenses' will include manual OD even if the invoice's auto AC entry already counted it, causing double-count whenever an OD entry's debit reproduces an invoice line. Recommend: when summing manual OD class-6, exclude those linked to an invoice (auto_generated=True && source_type='invoice').

routes/fiscal.py /expenses endpoint only returns invoices (line 453). The endpoint name and description mention 'factures + ecritures OD classe 6' but OD entries with class-6 lines are NOT included in the response — only invoices are. This is a divergence from the regularize endpoint which DOES include manual OD. Either expand /expenses to include OD entries OR rename to /invoice-expenses for clarity.

auto_entries.generate_bank_entry uses txn.get('account_number') or '550000' (line 212). When a manual transaction has no account_number set and no statement linkage, the entry posts to 550000 which is the parent collective banque account — bypassing the per-bank 550xxx sub-account. Recommend: at least try to inherit from txn.statement_id -> statements.account_number when txn.account_number is empty.

routes/accounting.py DELETE entry 400-blocks only when entry.auto_generated is True (line 188). It does NOT block entries with source_type='regularization' if some legacy entry was inserted without auto_generated=True. The regularize endpoint correctly sets auto_generated=True so this is OK today, but if anyone backfills regul entries via a script omitting that flag, they'd be deletable. Consider a defense-in-depth check on source_type too.

GET /api/fiscal/expenses lacks any RBAC decorator/middleware visible in fiscal.py — verified by test that owner gets 403, meaning the project-wide auth middleware on /api/fiscal applies the gate. Good, but worth noting it's enforced by middleware not route-level — any change to middleware path matching could expose this without test failure unless the RBAC test is rerun.
